# `combine-identical-switch-prongs`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: none · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports adjacent switch prongs with identical bodies and no payload capture.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

One comma-separated prong makes shared behavior explicit and removes duplicated
branch bodies.

## When it fires

Bodies must be textually identical, and no comment may sit above a prong,
inside it, or after it on its last line, because combining would drop or
misplace it. Captured payloads are excluded because their compatibility
requires type information. A run of adjacent identical prongs is reported once,
at its second prong.

Rows of a status table are left apart: prongs whose items are all
SCREAMING_CASE enum literals (`.NOENT`, `.ACCESS_DENIED`, the Zig mirrors of
C errno, NTSTATUS and Win32 error codes) and whose body is `unreachable`, an
error value or a `return`. Such tables list one status per line so they can be
checked against the platform's documentation and annotated per value.

The quick fix moves the case items of the whole run into the first prong's
list. It is withheld when a prong is `inline` or lists its items over several
lines or with a trailing comma.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn run(n: u8) u8 {
    return switch (n) {
        0 => 1,
        1 => 1,
        else => 2,
    };
}
```
